Code 57/3/1, SET-1, BIOLOGY (Theory), 3 hours, 70 marks); every ODD index 1-25 is the Hindi facing page. The contact sheet, full-size reads and a text-layer scan of every odd page (zero English function words on any of them) show no English overflow onto an odd page and no parity inversion; the last page, idx 26, is English (Q33). Born-digital: the text layer was a DRAFT only and every row was checked on the full-size page (the layer drops the Klinefelter/Down/Turner option text in Q6, the degree signs in Q7/Q9, the isotope superscripts in Q8, the whole of Q11/Q12's drawn options, half of Q17, Q19(b) and Q21(a), Q24's crosses and the 'one'/'two' quotes in Q25). Instruction (viii) names internal choice in Sections B, C and D only, but the paper also prints OR in all three Section E questions; seven alternatives in all (Q21, Q26, Q29(c), Q30(c), Q31, Q32, Q33), each confirmed against a bare OR in the marking scheme. Primary marks: A16 + B10 + C21 + D8 + E15 = 70. Section-A key read on the scheme IMAGE (ms p03, no SECTION A heading, key directly under the 'MARKING SCHEME ... [Paper Code: 57/3/1]' header) and on its text layer: CCBDCABCCABCABDC, 16 of 16 agree. One CBSE void, outside Section A: Q24(a), '1 mark is to be awarded to all the students if attempted'. Q29's DNA duplex is printed under sub-part (a) but sub-part (b) works on 'the same given DNA strand', so the duplex is carried in the shared context (the printed line of vertical base-pair bars between the two strands is omitted). No raised decimal dots on the paper. Quotes are straight, scientific names plain text (the Biology rules).

questions.stem: Which one of the following represents the correct annealing of primers to the DNA to be amplified in the PCR ?

options.label: A
options.text: Upper strand 5' to 3' and lower strand 3' to 5' (left to right); a 5'-3' primer paired at the left end of the upper strand and a 3'-5' primer paired at the right end of the lower strand

options.label: B
options.text: Upper strand 5' to 3' and lower strand 3' to 5' (left to right); a 3'-5' primer paired at the right end of the upper strand and a 5'-3' primer paired at the left end of the lower strand

options.label: C
options.text: Upper strand 3' to 5' and lower strand 5' to 3' (left to right); a 3'-5' primer paired at the left end of the upper strand and a 5'-3' primer paired at the right end of the lower strand

options.label: D
options.text: Upper strand 3' to 5' and lower strand 5' to 3' (left to right); a 3'-5' primer paired at the right end of the upper strand and a 5'-3' primer paired at the left end of the lower strand

questions._figure: REQUIRED:the four options ARE drawings: each is a pair of long parallel DNA strands with their 5' and 3' ends marked, and two short primers drawn as small ladders joined to one strand or the other, each primer's own 5' and 3' ends marked. The option texts above are a neutral, left-to-right reading of each panel (strand polarities, which strand each primer pairs with, at which end, and in which orientation); they name no rule, so the antiparallel-annealing principle still has to be supplied by the student. The drawn originals should be attached. Page idx 8.

questions.stem: The population growth curve applicable for a population growing in a geometric fashion, when the resources are not limiting in the habitat will be :

options.label: A
options.text: A horizontal line: population density stays constant with time

options.label: B
options.text: A straight line rising from the origin: population density increases at a steady rate with time

options.label: C
options.text: A curve rising from the origin and becoming steeper and steeper with time

options.label: D
options.text: A curve rising from near the origin, becoming steeper, then flattening out to a plateau

questions._figure: REQUIRED:the four options ARE graphs, each of Population density (vertical axis) against Time (horizontal axis, arrow pointing right), with no numbers on either axis. The option texts above are a neutral reading of the line each panel draws (flat, straight, ever-steepening, levelling off); they do not name the growth model, so the student still has to match geometric growth to its curve. The drawn originals should be attached. Page idx 8.

questions._figure: REQUIRED:three upright gel set-ups labelled Set-up A, Set-up B and Set-up C, each a tall rectangle with a well at its top end holding DNA fragments. questions.stem: Explain the IUI and IUT methods of assisted reproductive technologies.

Three crosses were carried out in pea plants with respect to flower colour violet/white (V/v) and flower position axial/terminal (A/a). Study in the table the crosses 'a', 'b' and 'c' where parental phenotypes and their \(\text{F}_1\) progeny phenotypes are given.
| Parental plants (Phenotypes) | \(\text{F}_1\) Progeny (Phenotypes) |
|---|---|
| (a) Violet, axial \(\times\) white, axial | 6/16 white, axial; 2/16 white, terminal; 6/16 violet, axial; 2/16 violet, axial |
| (b) Violet, axial \(\times\) white, terminal | 1/4 violet, axial; 1/4 violet, terminal; 1/4 white, axial; 1/4 white, terminal |
| (c) Violet, axial \(\times\) violet, axial | 3/4 violet, axial; 1/4 white, axial |
Find the genotypes of each of the parental pairs of crosses 'a', 'b' and 'c'.
questions._cbseVoided: (a) 1 mark is to be awarded to all the students if attempted, parental genotype is not possible to find from the given information.
questions._flag: Cross (a) prints '2/16 violet, axial' twice (6/16 and 2/16 of the same class) and no violet, terminal class, so its progeny cannot be explained; the intended fourth line is evidently '2/16 violet, terminal', which gives VvAa x vvAa. Transcribed as printed. The void covers part (a) only (1 of the 3 marks). Each cross's progeny lines are printed one per line inside a single table cell; they are joined here with semicolons.

(a) If the frequency of the recessive trait is 9% in population-one, work out the frequency of homozygous dominant and heterozygous dominant snakes.
(b) Name the mechanism of evolution that must have operated so that population-two evolved from population-one.
questions._figure: REQUIRED:a two-column box headed 'Population-one' and 'Population-two (Migration of Birds)', each column showing a group of drawn snakes on a sandy background, with two birds drawn in flight above the Population-two column. Part (a) is answerable from the stem's 9% alone, but (b) turns on how the mix of dark and light snakes differs between the two drawings, so the shade counts in each column are withheld here. Page idx 18.

Read the passage given below and answer the questions that follow.
In recombinant DNA technology, restriction enzymes are used as they recognize and cut DNA within a specific recognition sequence. BamH I is one such restriction enzyme which binds at the recognition sequence 5' G-G-A-T-C-C 3' and cleaves this sequence between G and G on each strand, whereas Alu I binds at the recognition sequence 5' A-G-C-T 3' and cleaves these sequences between G and C on each strand.
5' C – C – G – T – A – G – C – T – A – T – C – A – G – C – T – G – G 3'
3' G – G – C – A – T – C – G – A – T – A – G – T – C – G – A – C – C 5'
